correctness.rationale: The two sharp finiteness thresholds themselves are correct. The Lagrange column norm is bounded above by a binomial constant times its squared denominator inverse and below by that inverse from its leading coefficient. For fixed p>0 powers of a sum of N nonnegative terms are comparable with the sum of their powers. Thus the numerator density reduces to one-point chord exponents β−2p (the other pair factors are bounded); the integral is finite if β−2p>−1, even including multi-node collisions. A separated single-pair collision proves necessity and logarithmic divergence at equality. Conditional diagonalization of the Gaussian covariance compares the conditional loss moment to T^p for every p>0. Multiplication of rows by unit phases proves integer band-translation invariance, and cofactor orthogonality proves the stated unmodified CUE mean. However, the Finding's unqualified assertion that the error lacks finite variance at β=2 is false for the coefficient error e itself: it is centered with finite covariance τ²I_N in the unmodified CUE case. It is the squared error ||e||² whose variance is infinite, as the preceding moment thresholds correctly imply. Also, Step 5's exact two-node formula needs G≡1 (or an equivalent law of the gap). Under the stated general G it is false: at N=2, β=2, G=1+T⁻¹ lies between 1 and 2. Under the unmodified law E₀T=2 and E₀T⁻¹=3/4 by the elementary sine integrals, so the tilted mean is (2+1)/(1+3/4)=12/7, not 2. The checker was read, not executed; its reported 70 finite checks concern unmodified two-node moments, cofactor orthogonality and trace identities and do not test arbitrary G.
residual_risks: The failure flags the wording of the frozen finding and the unqualified exact two-node statement, not a counterexample to either finiteness threshold.

originality.rationale: The central claimed fractional-moment transition is an elementary consequence of the classical Morris circular Selberg integral. For W_j=∏_{i≠j}|z_i−z_j|⁻² the standard inverse Vandermonde coefficient formula gives ∑W_j≤T≤binom(2N−2,N−1)∑W_j. Thus finiteness is equivalent to that of the sum of the E[W_j^p]. The bounded positive weighting G gives equivalence of these integrals with G=1. In the latter ensemble fix z_j by rotation, then rotate the remaining nodes to place the fixed factor at −1. The unnormalized moment is exactly M_{N−1}(a,a,γ) of Forrester–Warnaar Eqs. (1.17)–(1.18), with a=(β−2p)/2 and γ=β/2. The classical admissibility condition is exactly β−2p>−1 for γ>0; outside it a single gap already diverges, with the remaining nodes in separate arcs. For N=2 this is the one-variable circle beta integral. This does not rely on any literal appearance of the Gram-trace wording in a prior paper: the standard coefficient formula gives two-sided comparability, not merely a one-way analogy. The bounded tilt and Gaussian extension are immediate comparisons, and the CUE first moment is explicitly known. No independently distinct original remainder of the frozen theorem was identified.
